decision: Founder ruled 2026-10-28 for event-driven trust recalculation with periodic reconciliation as a backup. Approve the implementation: which events trigger a restamp, who runs it, and the policy amendment it needs?
whyItMatters: The ruling is made but only its detection half is built. Restamping writes registry/named frontmatter and a timeline event, a Verifier-gated gaia dev mutation outside any Steward envelope, so the trigger and its authority need your approval before anything runs unattended.
evidence: The 22 stale stamps were corrected on main by PR #2147 using gaia dev calibrate-trust-magnitude, with no grade or star-level change.
Issue #1642 remains open for the recurring policy, not for those corrections.

Founder ruling 2026-10-28: event-driven recalculation with periodic reconciliation as backup; recomputing derived information is distinct from canonical trust, grade, star, evidence-assertion or policy mutation, which stay Class C.

Built (this PR): trust_stamp_stale observations now carry recomputationOnly (computed grade still agrees with the stored star level) and the exact gaia dev calibrate-trust-magnitude command. Periodic reconciliation already exists: the sensor re-measures every scan. Not built: the event trigger.

Proposed trigger: the same reviewed PR that changes evidence (gaia dev evidence, star refresh, ingest) runs calibrate-trust-magnitude for only the affected skills; a restamp that would move a star level is not a restamp and goes to the desk.
recommended: Approve: restamp only affected skills inside the PR that changes their evidence, with recomputationOnly as the gate; periodic reconciliation stays the backstop; any star, grade or policy movement stays Class C.
alternative: Keep restamping manual, run by a Verifier from the recomputationOnly findings.
unblocks: Retiring trust_stamp_stale debt without per-event founder work; the Class C debt kind stays for anything not recomputation-only.
